weeks.rule_text: Short vowel, one beat, ends in f, l, s or z: double it!

way1_script.title: Look at this word
way1_script.text: Grown-up: Say 'bell'. Show Anya the word. Ask: how many Ls do you see?

way1_script.title: Cover one L
way1_script.text: Cover the second L with your finger. Does it still say bell? Yes! So why two? Because it is SHORT, ONE BEAT, and ends in L. Double it!

way1_script.title: Now try off
way1_script.text: Same trick. Short o, one beat, ends in f. Double the f!

way1_script.title: Now try kiss
way1_script.text: Short i, one beat, ends in s. Double the s!

way1_script.title: Now try buzz
way1_script.text: Short u, one beat, ends in z. Double the z! Say the rule together: short vowel, one beat, ends in f-l-s-z, double it.

way1_script.title: Rule breakers
way1_script.text: Some words break the rule. Read them together: of, if, bus, gas, yes, us, this keep ONE letter. And help, milk: no doubling when another letter sits between the vowel and the end. We just remember the breakers.

way1_script.title: Your turn
way1_script.text: Grown-up: say each word. Anya writes it on paper.

quiz.q: Which word breaks the rule (one s)?

weeks.watch_for: 'bus' and 'of' are exceptions. Say so plainly: 'These two are rule-breakers. We just remember them.' The Rule breakers slide lists the rest (if, gas, yes, us, this).

exceptions.why: of has one f, and it even sounds like v!
if keeps one f.
bus has one s.
gas has one s.
yes has one s.
us has one s.
this has one s.
No double: the l is not right after the vowel.
No double: the k is not right after the vowel.

weeks.rule_text: Silent e makes the vowel say its name. Teams: ai in the middle, ay at the end, oa, ee.

way1_script.title: Magic e
way1_script.text: Say 'cap'. Now add a magic e at the end. The a says its name: cape! The e is silent but it is bossy.

way1_script.title: kit to kite
way1_script.text: Say 'kit'. Add the e. Now the i says its name: kite!

way1_script.title: rob to robe
way1_script.text: Say 'rob'. Add the e. Now the o says its name: robe!

way1_script.title: cub to cube
way1_script.text: Say 'cub'. Add the e. Now the u says its name: cube!

way1_script.title: Vowel teams
way1_script.text: Vowels can also hold hands. ai lives in the middle (train). ay lives at the end (play). oa says o (boat). ee says e (cheese).

way1_script.title: Rule breakers
way1_script.text: Some words have a magic e that does NOT work: have, give, live (words can't end in v). come, some, done, love: the o says u. And said: ai says e. Rule breakers! We keep them in our heart.

way1_script.title: Your turn
way1_script.text: Grown-up: say each word. Anya writes it on paper.

options: Makes the vowel say its name
quiz.answer: Makes the vowel say its name

quiz.q: Which word has a silent e?

way3_words.note: a_e is one split tile: the e reaches back to the a.

way4_game.prompt: Where does the long a live?

weeks.watch_for: Do not add ea vs ee this week. If she asks, say 'ee is our team this week'.

exceptions.why: The e is only there because words can't end in v. The a stays short.
Same trick: the i stays short.
The i stays short (I live here).
The o says u, not its name.
The o says u. A rule breaker!
The o says u. Another rule breaker.
The o says u here too.
ai says e here, not a. Just remember it.

weeks.rule_text: Bossy r changes the vowel: ar, or, ir, ur.

way1_script.title: Pirate arr!
way1_script.text: When r stands next to a vowel, r is the boss. a + r says ARR like a pirate. car, dark, farm.

way1_script.title: or says or
way1_script.text: o + r says OR, like fork. fork, born.

way1_script.title: ir says er
way1_script.text: i + r says ER. bird, first, stir are ir words.

way1_script.title: ur says er too
way1_script.text: u + r ALSO says ER. turn, hurt are ur words. Two spellings, one sound: we just learn which words are which.

way1_script.title: Four columns
way1_script.text: Sort them together: which column does each word go in?

way1_script.title: Rule breakers
way1_script.text: Watch out for w. After w, ar says or (war, warm) and or says er (word, work, worm). And er is a third spelling of the er sound (her).

way1_script.title: Your turn
way1_script.text: Grown-up: say each word. Anya writes it on paper.

quiz.q: After w, what does 'or' say in 'work'?
Which word has ar that says or?

way3_words.note: Rule breaker: or says er after w.

way4_game.prompt: Take a photo of a book page. Circle the bossy r words with your finger!

weeks.watch_for: Keep most 'er' words out this week; 'her' is shown once as the third spelling of the er sound. Watch the w words: war/warm (ar says or), word/work/worm (or says er).

exceptions.why: After w, ar says or.
After w, ar says or.
After w, or says er!
After w, or says er!
After w, or says er!
er is a third way to spell the er sound.

weeks.rule_text: igh says I. Little words end in -le.

way1_script.title: Three letters, one sound
way1_script.text: i-g-h is a team of three letters that makes ONE sound: I. The g and h are silent helpers. They hold the i's hand.

way1_script.title: Silent helpers
way1_script.text: Cover the g and h. It still says I. Now uncover them. We need them for the spelling!

way1_script.title: More igh words
way1_script.text: high, right, fight. Say each one and find the igh.

way1_script.title: Clap lit-tle
way1_script.text: Clap the beats: lit-tle. Two claps! The last beat is a consonant plus le. Little has a double t, just like our FLOSS words.

way1_script.title: Clap ap-ple
way1_script.text: ap-ple. Two claps! The end is p + le.

way1_script.title: Rule breakers
way1_script.text: The I sound has other spellings: y at the end (my, fly), just i (find), ie (pie). And some words end in el, al, il instead of le: camel, towel, animal, pencil. table has a long a, so no double letter before le.

way1_script.title: Your turn
way1_script.text: Grown-up: say each word. Anya writes it on paper.

quiz.q: How many letters make the igh sound?
Which letters are the silent helpers?
Which word says I without igh?
Which word does NOT end in -le?

weeks.watch_for: 'little' has a double t. Link it back to Week 1: 'remember the FLOSS rule? Double letters again!'

exceptions.why: At the end of a word, y can say I.
y says I at the end.
Sometimes just i says I.
ie can say I too.
Ends in el, not le.
Ends in el, not le.
Ends in al, not le.
Ends in il, not le.
Long a, so no double letter before le.

weeks.rule_text: Heart words: you just have to know them by heart.

way1_script.title: Heart words
way1_script.text: Some words do not follow the rules. We keep them in our heart. Here is the routine: 1 tap the sounds, 2 put them in boxes, 3 write the normal parts, 4 draw a heart over the naughty part.

way1_script.title: Today's word 1
way1_script.text: Tap the sounds. Which part is naughty? Draw a heart over it.

way1_script.title: Today's word 2
way1_script.text: Tap the sounds. Which part is naughty? Draw a heart over it.

way1_script.title: Rule breakers
way1_script.text: Sound-alike traps: there / their (their = belongs to them), were / where (where = which place), some / sum (a maths sum). And home follows the magic e rule, but come does not!

way1_script.title: Your turn
way1_script.text: Grown-up: say each word. Anya writes it on paper and draws the heart.

quiz.q: Which part of 'said' is the heart part?

way4_game.prompt: Take a photo of your own writing. Tap every heart word you find!

weeks.watch_for: 'because' mnemonic: Big Elephants Can Always Understand Small Elephants. Only if still needed by Wednesday.

exceptions.why: Sounds like there, but means 'belongs to them'.
Sounds like were, but asks 'which place?'
Sounds like some, but it is a maths sum.
home follows the magic e rule. come does not!

weeks.rule_text: All the rules together. Which rule does this word follow?
weeks.watch_for: No new rule. Before each word she taps which rule it belongs to. Do not correct the tap; just note it.
